newsitem.title: USA: AIG Q2 worldwide life premiums up.
newsitem.headline: AIG Q2 worldwide life premiums up.

text.p: American International Group Inc said Thursday that second quarter worldwide life insurance net premiums written rose 13 percent from a year earlier after the impact of foreign exchange.
Before the foreign exchange impact, worldwide life insurance net premiums written rose 17.5 percent.
"Our life operations in Asia, Central Europe and Latin America all reported strong results," AIG Chairman Maurice Greenberg said in a statement.
"Life operations in Russia have commenced, and we recently received a license to operate a wholly owned life company in Uruguay," he added.

In the United States, AIG's growing life business continued to report strong results. Life insurance premium income rose 13.0 percent in the quarter, to $2.55 billion from $2.25 billion a year ago, AIG said.
In financial services, second quarter pretax operating income rose 30.8 percent, to $173.6 million from $132.7 million.
"International Lease Finance Corp (ILFC) had an excellent quarter, as it benefited from higher lease rates and strong aircraft sales," Greenberg said.
"Both AIG Financial Products Corp and AIG Trading Group Inc reported outstanding performance," he added.
In asset management, he said AIG has many new initiatives under way, both in direct investment activities and infrastructure funds.
In Japan, AIG's joint venture with Mitsubishi Trust and Banking Corp in investment management, announced earlier this year, became fully licensed in the quarter.
"Recent currency devaluations in Thailand and the Philippines will have an immaterial effect on earnings," Greenberg said.
AIG continued its program to repurchase shares of its common stock in the open market in the second quarter.
In the 1997 first half it repurchased about 2.3 million shares.
